{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The core risk-allocation provisions are strong for us and require no redlining: Vendor's IP and data indemnity (§ 20), ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data (§ 13–15), the mutual liability cap with uncapped Excluded Claims (§ 21), assignment and change-of-control (§ 24), licence scope (§ 13), governing law and venue in New York (§ 28), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), the performance warranty (§ 19), and Vendor insurance (§ 18). Section 2.1 also confirms there is no minimum purchase commitment, and § 12.3 preserves our competitive freedom.

Six items require action, and each sits in walk-away territory under the playbook. Five are drafted obligations running against us — full-term sourcing exclusivity (§ 2.2), USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages (§ 7.6), an open-ended Customer-side MFN (§ 7.2), unannounced Vendor audits with remote access to our systems (§ 22.1), and a 180-day non-renewal notice window (§ 8.2) — plus the absence of any convenience termination right for Customer across a three-year term. A seventh item, the one-way 18-month non-solicit/no-engage in § 12.4, fails the fallback on every material term. Notably, §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 each contradict § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, most-favoured-customer or no-hire commitment; fixing them removes internal inconsistency as well as risk.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (with §§ 20.2–20.5, 21.3) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 13.2 (with §§ 14.1–14.4, 15.1) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.3, 18.2) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.4) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 8.1 (no clause in § 9) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with §§ 28.2–28.3) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Compliant | § 2.1 (with §§ 7.1, 12.3) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | **Deviation** | § 8.2 |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (with §§ 11.2–11.3) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with §§ 19.2–19.5) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) |

---

## Walk-away items

The following six findings fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **§ 2.2 — Full-term sole and exclusive provider commitment.** No category limitation beyond hosted analytics, no 12-month cap, no exit on service-level or delivery failure; fails the fallback on every element and conflicts with §§ 2.1 and 12.3. *Proposal: convert to a non-exclusive appointment with no Customer exclusivity obligation.*
2. **§ 7.6 — USD 25,000 per day liquidated damages payable by Customer.** Triggered by any dependency delay, however minor, and uncapped in duration, so accrual can exceed remaining contract value; the mutual cap in § 21.1 does not cure it. *Proposal: delete and confirm Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalties.*
3. **§ 7.2 — Customer-side MFN.** Open-ended: no defined product, no duration limit, no like-for-like carve-outs; contradicts § 12.3. *Proposal: negate the Customer-side MFN obligation.*
4. **§ 22.1 — Unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems.** No frequency cap, no notice period, and the remote-access permission conflicts with § 22.3. §§ 22.2–22.3 are already protective on cost and system access. *Proposal: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site, independent confidential auditor; delete remote access.*
5. **T4C — No convenience termination right for Customer.** Section 9 provides only for-cause exits (material breach, insolvency, Vendor default), with § 27.3 force majeure and §§ 6.2/19.4/20.5 remedy-specific; nothing covers convenience across the three-year term in § 8.1. *Proposal: insert § 9.4 — 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right during a committed term.*
6. **§ 8.2 — 180-day non-renewal notice window.** Exceeds the 90-day walk-away threshold and the 60-day fallback. *Proposal: shorten to sixty (60) days. The 12-month renewal term and the § 8.3 pricing limb (lesser of CPI and 3%) already meet the checklist and are not flagged.*

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redlines** for the six walk-away items above, plus § 12.4, in a single markup. For § 12.4 we take the preferred position — removal of any Customer non-solicitation restriction — and offer the narrow mutual fallback (personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of that involvement, solicitation only, with a general-advertising carve-out) in the comment.
2. **Flag the internal inconsistencies** to Vendor in the cover note: §§ 2.2, 7.2 and 12.4 each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3, and § 22.1's remote-access permission contradicts § 22.3. Our edits resolve all four.
3. **Confirm no reopening of compliant clauses.** We will not seek changes to §§ 11, 13–15, 18–21, 24 or 28. Two points are noted for the record only, not redlined: Deliverable ownership in § 14.2 is subject to payment of applicable Fees, and the § 21.3 payment carve-out is limited to undisputed Fees for conforming Services.
4. **Sequence the negotiation** by treating the § 7.6 daily liquidated damages and the § 2.2 exclusivity as non-negotiable removals, with the audit, MFN, renewal-window and convenience-termination edits presented as conforming changes to the playbook fallback or preferred position.
5. **Report back** on Vendor's response to the § 8.2 window and the inserted § 9.4, as those two drive our exit optionality across the three-year term."}
